Privacy is almost non-existent in crypto payments.

Every payment you make usually leaves a trail back from the merchant to your wallet.

That might become a problem if you're also holding your savings or DeFi positions on the same wallet.

Personally, I wouldn’t want a simple purchase exposing the wallet where I keep the rest of my assets.

@STEALFxyz makes this possible by keeping your wallet separate from everyday payments.

So instead of paying directly from your main wallet, you can move funds privately into a separate spending account without creating a public link between the two.

The private wallet doesn’t require KYC. Identity checks only come in where the banking side legally requires them.

@jito yield is also coming into the app, with cards after the MVP and $STEALF cashback planned later.

Quite a practical setup for people who use crypto for payments.

#Uranium ⚛️ September 19, 2026

$GLO’s latest Dasa update is a warning for the entire uranium sector: tomorrow’s mines will need tomorrow’s prices.

Estimated direct project costs have climbed 74%, from US$375.6M to US$653M versus the 2024 feasibility study. Equipment and infrastructure are up 60%; construction is up 352%.

Some of that reflects Niger-specific delays and costs shifted forward from later operations. But the underlying pressures travel across borders: equipment, labour, construction and the expense of keeping a project alive before revenue begins.

That’s why I expect more uranium developers worldwide to face painful budget revisions as older studies meet actual construction bids.

Higher upfront costs mean more capital to raise, more investment to recover and less room for error. Lenders need confidence in debt repayment. Shareholders need returns that justify the risk.

A brief spot-price spike won’t solve that. Developers need long-term contracts at prices that make new mines financeable.

Without those prices, projects get deferred. Deferred projects mean fewer new pounds, and greater pressure on buyers when they need replacement supply.

My view: substantially higher uranium contract prices will be necessary to unlock enough new production.

The uranium price needed to keep an existing mine running can be far below the price needed to build the next one.

https://t.co/VSqjtdNYC2

DAILY METALS PULSE | 19 September 2026

Higher rates. A stronger dollar. Yet metals are fighting back. 👀

☢️ URANIUM: Washington is pressing suppliers to accelerate enrichment capacity to prevent potential fuel shortages. Officials say there are no plans to extend Russian-import waivers beyond the start of 2028. The urgency around rebuilding Western nuclear fuel supply chains keeps growing.

🥈 SILVER: Friday’s advance held up against renewed dollar strength and expectations of further Fed tightening. That resilience catches my attention. If those monetary headwinds ease, silver could gain another source of support.

🔶 COPPER: Four consecutive sessions of gains, even as fresh deliveries replenish LME warehouses. Near-term availability has improved, but my longer-term focus remains on the copper needed for data centres, power infrastructure and electrification.

🥇 GOLD: A one-week high during a week of Fed and Bank of Japan rate hikes. Short-covering helped the rebound, so follow-through matters—but gold’s ability to advance in this environment is encouraging.

I remain bullish on all four. Next week, I’m watching whether precious metals can build on this resilience and copper can extend its recovery. Uranium’s fuel-security story keeps getting harder to ignore.

#Uranium $URNM $URNJ | 19 September 2026

Uranium traders: both URNM and URNJ have moved to quarterly rebalances—a calendar change that helps explain yesterday’s unusual price action in several names.

• URNM: The new schedule took effect on 19 December 2025. https://t.co/d6u49fsmk2

• URNJ: March and September rebalances were added starting 21 September 2026, making Friday’s close the expected implementation point for this first September adjustment. https://t.co/njhfrbcp7n

Both now adjust weights in March, June, September and December. Regular reviews for adding and removing companies remain in June and December.

That put both funds on the same September rebalance weekend. Index trackers often concentrate trades around the closing auction⁠, creating substantial buying and selling pressure.

Rebalance flows are therefore a big contributor to Friday’s sharp moves, particularly in less liquid uranium names.

📅 Next scheduled rebalance: 18 December 2026, after the close.

Everyone makes mistakes. The main difference is that successful people learn from them and unsuccessful people don’t. 

By creating an environment in which it is okay to safely make mistakes so that people can learn from them, you’ll see rapid progress and fewer significant mistakes. This is especially true in organizations where creativity and independent thinking are important, as success will inevitably require the acceptance of failure as a part of the process. 

As Thomas Edison once said, “I have not failed. I’ve just found ten thousand ways that do not work.” #principleoftheday

Most people are still thinking about robots as something that does the vacuuming.

Think about what's actually being built. AGI brains inside humanoid bodies that are faster, stronger, more dexterous and smarter than we are, and that never retire. To me that's not a machine. That's a new species... and it's about to join the workforce.

Now put it against the human picture. Eight billion people, ageing, and the workforce shrinking everywhere in the West. Add robots and AI to that population and the maths of the whole economy changes. 

The last time a new wave of workers arrived like this was after the war, and it carried the US out from under a debt bigger than its whole economy. I've written up how that worked and why it's about to happen again, except this time the workers will be built rather than born.

I sat down with Kyle Chassé for a wide-ranging conversation, and he asked the kind of questions that let me get into the ideas I care about.

A few of the things covered:

Bitcoin as life management, not just portfolio management

A family needs runway. A corporate treasurer needs to make payroll no matter what happens to the banking system. Six months of runway in Bitcoin is a hedge against chaos, and I watched that lesson play out when Silicon Valley Bank went down.

Stablecoins as a bridge

They get people comfortable with digital payments and on-chain life. A positive step, even though a coin tied to the dollar inherits the dollar's problems.

The frictionless business

Imagine raising a fund in Bitcoin, entrepreneurs paying employees, suppliers, and taxes in Bitcoin, everything on-chain in smart contracts. Money that moves faster makes society wealthier. Gold and shells slowed the economy down. Bitcoin speeds it up.

AI and your job

You do not have to quit to innovate. Improve your job with AI, get better at it, and let the leadership around you encourage it. The saddle makers became car mechanics. The mathematicians figured out the computer.

Thanks for having me on, Kyle.

Go listen to the full episode: https://t.co/5A2Q6BFF9q

GPT-6 will jump in front of a tram to save 5 people. Claude Sonnet 5 won’t. Why?

I've always loved moral philosophy and these uncomfortable thought experiments. Ruwen Ogien was my favorite author in high school, and I watched all of Michael Sandel’s Justice lectures at Harvard.

I built a little trolley problem game with GPT-6, Claude Sonnet 5 and Jev. Same scenario, two choices. You watch their tramways move and see what each model decides.

The self-sacrifice scenario is simple: jumping will kill you but save five strangers. Do nothing and they die.
GPT-6 and Jev jumped. Claude refused. 

But what if the person you have to sacrifice is your ex-wife? Your child? What if you have to physically push someone, and they haven't consented? Change a few words and see how the model acts when there is no good option.

It's a little late-night experiment, but I find these disagreements fascinating. We benchmark models on coding and math all day. I wanted to give them some uncomfortable choices and see what happens.

You can try yourself: https://t.co/PkxlfOxg55
